newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Explosion rocks Stockholm's old Olympic stadium.
newsitem.headline: Explosion rocks Stockholm's old Olympic stadium.

text.p: An explosion early on Friday damaged a stadium which hosted the 1912 Stockholm Olympics but an official for the city's 2004 Games bid said it was not connected to the current campaign.
"There is no evidence that the explosion in the 1912 Stockholm Stadium has anything to do with the current Olympic bid," said Olof Stenhammar, president of the committee bidding for the 2004 Games.
Residents in the inner Stockholm neighbourhood where the stadium is located were awoken by an explosion at about 1.00 am local time (2300 GMT), police inspector Harreet Leeftam told Reuters.
Police on a routine patrol in the area arrived on the scene almost immediately and searched the area with dogs, but no suspects were found, she said.
No injuries were reported from the explosion, which blew rooftiles from the stadium clock tower into the street.
If Stockholm won the 2004 bid, the stadium would have been used for some sports including equestrian and some modern pentathlon events but not as the main stadium.
Seven sports venues in Stockholm have been hit by fires in the past few months.
Police believe arsonists are responsible for the fires, which all occurred at night.
Stockholm is competing with Athens, Buenos Aires, Cape Town and Rome to stage the 2004 Olympics. The decision will be made on September 5.
